home-remodeling.local_heading: Remodeling south of the New River
intro_paragraphs: Rio Vista was platted in 1920 and built in two waves. The first left Mediterranean Revival and Spanish Colonial houses on Ponce de Leon Drive and Cordova Road, with barrel tile, arched openings and plaster walls. The second filled the Rio Vista Isles finger streets after the war with ranches and split-levels, most of them sitting on wide lots under oaks that are now older than the mortgages. Owners here rarely tear these down. They gut them: new plan, new systems, same roofline, same address on the same canal.

The permitting authority here is Fort Lauderdale's Development Services Department, and since the city moved to digital intake, drawings and revisions travel through the LauderBuild portal instead of a counter. Broward adds a layer Miami-Dade homeowners never see: the Board of Rules and Appeals, which certifies Broward building departments and their inspectors, maintains the county's amendments to the Florida Building Code, and settles disputed interpretations. Broward also sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every window, door and roof assembly you install needs an HVHZ product approval in the permit file.

The experience behind that is 20-plus years in South Florida and more than 150 remodels and additions delivered, every one permitted and inspected. On a street like North Rio Vista Boulevard that translates into practical things: a fixed written scope before demolition, a supervisor here every working day, dust barriers and floor protection that treat the finished half of the house as finished, and deliveries staged so the neighbors can still get out of their driveways. One accountable team runs the job from estimate to warranty. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: Scope of a Rio Vista rebuild
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets opened before the scope is written down. Here is what a Rio Vista whole-home remodel most often includes.

scope_items.name: Plan changes, structurally
scope_items.desc: Removing bearing walls in 1920s masonry and postwar block, with beams sized by an engineer, sealed drawings, and inspections at every step.

scope_items.name: Plumbing, power and air
scope_items.desc: New service and panels, repiped supply and drain lines, ducted air handling, and low-voltage runs pulled while the walls are still open.

scope_items.name: HVHZ windows and doors
scope_items.desc: Impact glass carrying High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals, detailed into old openings so a 1926 elevation does not end up looking like a storefront.

scope_items.name: Millwork and finishes
scope_items.desc: Custom cabinetry, stone, interior doors and trim scaled to the ceiling heights you actually have, finished to survive year-round humidity off the water.

scope_items.name: Roof, stucco and exterior
scope_items.desc: Re-roof coordination, stucco repair and paint sequenced with the interior work so scaffolding goes up once and the street sees one project.

faqs.q: Is my 1920s Rio Vista house worth gutting, or should I start over?
faqs.a: For most of these houses, remodeling wins. The original masonry, the roof pitch, the lot placement and the mature canopy are hard to replicate, and a teardown restarts your zoning, flood elevation and setback obligations from zero. A full gut lets you keep the shell and the street presence while replacing plan, systems and openings. Where the structure is genuinely compromised we will say so early, with an engineer's opinion rather than ours alone.

faqs.q: People keep mentioning BORA. Who are they and why should I care?
faqs.a: The Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals sits between the state code and your inspector. It certifies the building officials and inspectors who will review a Rio Vista permit, maintains the county's amendments to the Florida Building Code, and rules on interpretations when officials disagree. You never file anything with them. The practical effect is that Broward enforces a rulebook Miami-Dade does not use, and your contractor should already know the difference.

faqs.q: We are in a flood zone. Does that cap how much remodeling we can do?
faqs.a: It can shape it. Much of Rio Vista sits in a special flood hazard area, and the city's floodplain administrator applies the federal substantial improvement test: once the cost of the work crosses half the market value of the structure, the whole building has to be brought into current flood compliance. That analysis belongs at the front of the project, alongside an elevation certificate, not in the middle of demolition. We run it before drawings are finalized.

faqs.q: Where do families live while the house is gutted?
faqs.a: Usually not for the heavy phase, and we would rather tell you that up front. When ceilings are open, the panel is out and there is no working kitchen, living on site is unpleasant and slows the crew down. Some Rio Vista projects phase well enough to keep a wing or a guest house occupied, with sealed barriers and separate access. We settle that question at the estimate so nobody is packing boxes in week three.

faqs.q: Where does the money actually go on a whole-home remodel?
faqs.a: Structure, systems and openings usually take more of the budget than anyone expects, because they are invisible when finished. Impact glass, a new electrical service, repiping and engineered beams are not selections you get to skip. Finishes then move the number as far as you want to take them. Rather than publish a per-foot figure that means nothing on your specific house, we walk it, scope it, and hand you a fixed written price tied to a specification.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the plans, the wish list, or just a set of frustrations. What comes back is a priced scope you can plan a year around, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodeling in Rio Vista, Fort Lauderdale FL
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Rio Vista kitchen remodeling in Fort Lauderdale. We move the kitchen to the canal side and permit every bit of it. Call (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and reworked layouts for Rio Vista kitchens, including the wall you want removed, permitted through Fort Lauderdale Building Services and run daily by a licensed, insured general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The kitchen is on the wrong side
intro_paragraphs: Rio Vista kitchens tend to be in the wrong place. The 1920s houses along Cordova Road and Ponce de Leon Drive put cooking in a closed rear room with one small window and a delivery door, and the postwar houses on the Rio Vista Isles canals were not much more generous. Everything worth looking at, meaning the dock, the pool and the afternoon light on the water, sits on the other side of a wall. Which is why a kitchen project here is usually a relocation with cabinetry attached.

Here is the good news about Rio Vista: it is not one of Fort Lauderdale's designated historic districts, and the Rio Vista Civic Association is a neighborhood organization rather than a design board with permit authority. An interior kitchen goes straight to Fort Lauderdale Building Services through LauderBuild for building, plumbing, electrical and mechanical permits, with inspections at rough and final. Gas, whether piped or propane, gets its own permit. Punch a new opening through an exterior wall and you add structural review plus an HVHZ-approved unit.

PGX runs kitchens in a specific order: cabinets ordered early, demolition timed to their arrival, stone templated after the boxes are set and level, appliances confirmed before anyone runs a circuit. You get a fixed written scope, a supervisor on site daily, and hard protection over floors and stair treads on the way in. Twenty-plus years in South Florida and more than 150 remodels and additions delivered, all of them permitted and inspected, under Lic. CGC1539072. The rest of your house stays a house while we work.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Priced line by line before demolition, so the number you sign is tied to a specification and not to a mood board.

scope_items.name: Built-to-order cabinetry
scope_items.desc: Cabinet packages made to your dimensions, with finishes and hardware chosen to hold up in a house that lives with its doors open.

scope_items.name: Stone on a real island
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble or porcelain slabs templated on set cabinets, with island framing engineered for the load and the seating overhang.

scope_items.name: Moving the kitchen
scope_items.desc: Relocating the room toward the water: new drain lines through slab, rerouted supply, engineered beams where a wall used to carry the roof.

scope_items.name: Appliances and venting
scope_items.desc: Hoods vented to the outside through detailed wall penetrations, plus dedicated circuits, water lines and gas runs permitted and inspected properly.

scope_items.name: Panel and lighting work
scope_items.desc: Service upgrades that older Rio Vista houses often need, then layered lighting so the island, the sink and the walkway each get their own.

faqs.q: Rio Vista is not a historic district. Does that make permitting easier?
faqs.a: It removes one layer. The neighborhood is old enough to feel like one, but it carries no local historic district designation, so a kitchen remodel does not need a certificate of appropriateness the way work on an individually designated landmark would. You still need building, plumbing, electrical and mechanical permits from Fort Lauderdale, and the inspections that come with them. Simpler path, same code.

faqs.q: Can we move the kitchen to the canal side of the house?
faqs.a: Often, yes, and it is the single change that transforms these houses. It means new drain lines cut into the slab and sloped correctly, supply and gas rerouted, and usually a structural beam where a wall is coming out. On a waterfront elevation it can also mean a new or enlarged opening, which brings HVHZ-approved glass and engineering into the permit set. Feasible, not trivial, and worth pricing before you fall in love with it.

faqs.q: Will our existing electrical panel handle a new appliance package?
faqs.a: In a lot of Rio Vista houses, no. Induction cooktops, double ovens, wine storage, a dishwasher drawer and under-cabinet everything add up fast, and panels installed decades ago were never sized for it. We have the load calculated during design rather than discovered at rough inspection, and if a service upgrade is needed it goes into the same permit package instead of arriving later as a surprise line item.

faqs.q: Where are we supposed to cook while this is happening?
faqs.a: Somewhere we set up before demolition day, usually a laundry room, garage corner or covered terrace with a sink, a fridge and a working circuit. Expect months rather than weeks, and blame the cabinets: custom millwork carries a long lead time, so we order it first and time demolition to its delivery instead of tearing the room out and waiting. Structural openings or a relocation stretch that further.

faqs.q: What pushes a Rio Vista kitchen budget up or down?
faqs.a: Three things, mostly: cabinetry construction, the stone you choose, and whether the room stays where it is. Appliances then do what appliances do. Moving plumbing through a slab and opening a bearing wall are the items that quietly separate a refresh from a project. We are a high-end contractor and rarely the lowest of three numbers; what we offer instead is a scope detailed enough that the price holds.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Walk us through how you cook and what annoys you. A fixed written estimate comes back, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodels for Rio Vista Homes, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Rio Vista bath remodels in Fort Lauderdale: a primary suite carved from an old plan, waterproofing tested before tile. (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, guest baths and powder rooms across Rio Vista, from Cordova Road to the Isles canals, permitted, inspected, waterproofed to spec, and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: One bathroom was the original plan
intro_paragraphs: Count the bathrooms in an unrenovated Rio Vista house and the era gives itself away. The 1920s places were drawn with a single full bath and maybe a half bath off the kitchen. The 1950s and 1960s houses out on the Isles added a second, usually shared through a hall, both of them tiled in colors that have since become collectible. What owners want now is a primary suite: a real shower, a double vanity, storage, and a door that closes on the rest of the house.

Fort Lauderdale Building Services permits the plumbing, electrical and mechanical work through LauderBuild, and inspectors want to see rough-in and waterproofing before anything gets covered. That sequence exists for a reason. Most of these houses sit on slab, so moving a drain means cutting concrete, re-sloping and re-pouring, and the inspection record is the only proof the work was done right. Broward's amendments to the Florida Building Code, administered through the county Board of Rules and Appeals, govern the details, and any new exterior window needs an HVHZ product approval.

Water finds whichever detail nobody checked, so we check all of them. Shower pans are flood-tested and left to sit before tile touches them, slopes are verified with a level rather than a feeling, blocking goes in before heavy glass is ordered, and exhaust actually reaches the outside instead of the attic. The scope is fixed in writing, a supervisor is on site every working day, and the route from your front door to the work zone gets protected. Licensed, insured, 150-plus projects deep.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: Every layer of a Rio Vista bath
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Fixtures are the easy part. These are the items that decide whether the room still looks new in ten years.

scope_items.name: Carving out a primary suite
scope_items.desc: Borrowing a bedroom, closet or hall bath to build one proper suite, laid out and permitted so a two-bath house finally has somewhere to get ready.

scope_items.name: Waterproofing, then tile
scope_items.desc: Bonded membranes, flood tests held overnight, linear drains set true, and curbless entries where the slab can be recessed without a fight.

scope_items.name: Stone, glass and tubs
scope_items.desc: Slab walls and freestanding tubs set on verified structure, with heavy frameless glass hung on real blocking rather than whatever the wall offers.

scope_items.name: Cast iron out, PVC in
scope_items.desc: Cast iron and galvanized lines swapped out while the floor is open, because access is free now and expensive once the marble is down.

scope_items.name: Air, light and hardware
scope_items.desc: A fan that reaches the outdoors, marine-grade hardware for canal air, and light at the mirror so the shower door still swings freely in year five.

faqs.q: We only have two bathrooms. How do we get a primary suite out of that?
faqs.a: Usually by borrowing. A small fourth bedroom, an oversized hall closet or a rear porch that was enclosed at some point can supply the square footage, and the hall bath gets rebuilt as the guest bath. On a Rio Vista lot with room to spare, a modest rear bump-out is sometimes cheaper than reorganizing the whole plan. We sketch both options with numbers attached so the decision is yours, not the drawing's.

faqs.q: Which inspections does a Fort Lauderdale bathroom remodel actually go through?
faqs.a: More than most people expect, and that is the point. Depending on scope you will see plumbing rough, electrical rough, mechanical for the exhaust, a shower pan or flood test, and finals for each trade. Fort Lauderdale schedules them through its permitting system, and nothing gets covered until the relevant one passes. We manage the calendar so inspectors are not the reason your tile setter is standing around.

faqs.q: What happens when you open the floor and find old cast iron?
faqs.a: We tell you the same day and show you the camera footage. In houses of this age under a slab, cast iron and galvanized pipe are commonly at the end of their service life, and running a new bathroom into a failing line is a poor trade. Where we can, we scope the inspection before demolition so replacement is priced in the original contract rather than added as a change order nobody planned for.

faqs.q: Does living on a canal change how you build a bathroom?
faqs.a: It changes what we specify. Air near the New River and the Isles canals is salt-laden and humid year-round, which is unkind to plated hardware, cheap hinges, unsealed stone and undersized exhaust fans. We use moisture-rated fixtures, ventilation sized to the room and ducted properly outside, and finishes chosen for coastal exposure. It costs a little more at selection and saves you a rebuild in a few years.

faqs.q: How much of the budget disappears behind the tile?
faqs.a: More than the showroom suggests. Demolition, slab cutting, new drain and supply lines, waterproofing, framing and blocking, ventilation and electrical usually account for a serious share of a high-end bath, and none of it photographs well. Stone, glass and fixtures then set the ceiling. We would rather scope the invisible half honestly and give you one fixed written number than quote low and discover the rest in week two.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and tell us what it should become. A fixed scope and an honest price follow, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Building an Addition in Rio Vista, Fort Lauderdale FL
home-additions.meta_description: Additions for Rio Vista homes in Fort Lauderdale. Extend to the rear, build a second floor, add a guest wing. Zoning and flood rules handled. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: More house on the same lot
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, garage conversions and guest suites for Rio Vista homes, engineered and zoned, permitted through the City of Fort Lauderdale, and built under daily supervision by a licensed general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Growing a house between two waterways
intro_paragraphs: Additions happen in Rio Vista because the alternative is leaving, and nobody leaves a street like this willingly. The same few projects come up again and again: a rear extension pushing a family room and primary suite toward the canal on the Rio Vista Isles streets, a second story over a 1950s ranch near Hector Park, a garage converted into a guest suite off Cordova Road, an in-law wing for a household that keeps growing in both directions. The work is making the new part look like it never was.

Fort Lauderdale reviews additions against its Unified Land Development Regulations before the building permit ever opens. Rio Vista is single-family zoned, and the district your lot sits in fixes the setbacks, the lot coverage and the height you have to build inside; anything reaching toward a canal also answers to the city's waterway standards. Variances go to the Board of Adjustment, not to a design board, since Rio Vista is not a designated historic district. On flood-zone parcels the city's floodplain administrator applies the federal substantial improvement test, which can reshape a project before it is drawn. Structural engineering and HVHZ approvals are assumed.

The hard parts of an addition are the joints. New footings have to meet old ones without arguing, tie-beams and roof framing have to land where the engineer drew them, and the stucco and tile have to age into the original rather than announce themselves. PGX handles that seam work directly, keeps the occupied side of the house sealed and usable, and runs a quiet site on a street where everyone knows everyone. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, one team from feasibility through warranty, under Lic. CGC1539072.
home-additions.scope_heading: Ways a Rio Vista house grows
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition begins with engineering and a zoning read. These five cover most of what gets built on these blocks.

scope_items.name: Extending into the back yard
scope_items.desc: Family rooms and primary suites pushed toward the canal, with the footings, tie-beam and roof connection detailed by an engineer and permitted together.

scope_items.name: A floor above the ranch
scope_items.desc: The existing block and footings get evaluated first, then an upper floor designed to live inside the district height limit and the neighbors' sightlines.

scope_items.name: Garages made habitable
scope_items.desc: Converting covered parking into conditioned space with insulation, HVHZ openings and permitted mechanical work that holds up when the house sells.

scope_items.name: Guest and in-law suites
scope_items.desc: Independent suites with bath, kitchenette and their own entry, built to code and proportioned to the original house instead of bolted to it.

scope_items.name: What sits underneath
scope_items.desc: Soil conditions, new footings, underpinning where required, and steel sized by an engineer, because a Rio Vista water table does not negotiate.

faqs.q: Will the city let me put a second story on a Rio Vista ranch?
faqs.a: Zoning usually allows it. Fort Lauderdale's single-family districts cap height, and a well-drawn second floor generally fits inside that ceiling; we confirm the number for your specific parcel before anyone sketches. The real question is structural: an engineer evaluates the existing block walls and footings and specifies reinforcement, new columns or upgraded tie-beams where needed. Occasionally the honest answer is that going out beats going up. We put both options in front of you with numbers.

faqs.q: How close to the seawall can a new addition sit?
faqs.a: Rarely as close as the sketch assumes. Fort Lauderdale's land development regulations set yard requirements measured from the property line along the waterway, and on the Rio Vista Isles streets that line often lands at or near the seawall itself. Factor in flood elevation and the usable envelope narrows again. We order a current survey and run the zoning math before anyone draws elevations, so what you see on paper is what the city can actually issue.

faqs.q: Everyone mentions the 50 percent rule. Does it apply to my house?
faqs.a: It applies if your property sits in the special flood hazard area, which covers a lot of Rio Vista. When the cost of an improvement reaches half the market value of the existing structure, the city's floodplain administrator requires the entire building to meet current flood standards, which for older slab homes can mean elevating. That is not automatically a dealbreaker, but it belongs in the first conversation, not the fourth. We check it against your elevation certificate early.

faqs.q: Is there an architectural review board in Rio Vista I have to satisfy?
faqs.a: No. Rio Vista has not been designated a historic district, and the Rio Vista Civic Association is a neighborhood organization rather than a permitting authority. If your particular house carries an individual historic designation, the city's Historic Preservation Board reviews exterior changes and issues a certificate of appropriateness. For everyone else, the path is zoning review and then the building permit.

faqs.q: Realistically, how long from first meeting to moving into the new room?
faqs.a: Assume the front end takes months. Design, survey, structural engineering, zoning review and permitting all happen before anyone digs, and a substantial addition then runs several more months in construction. A year from first conversation to furniture is a fair expectation for a serious rear extension or second story. The schedule is written into the contract, and when reality argues with it, we revise it in writing rather than by phone.

outdoor-living.meta_description: Terraces, summer kitchens and pool decks in Rio Vista, Fort Lauderdale — built for canal-front life and salt air, fully permitted. Call (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: The dock end of the house
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Covered terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas and pool decks for Rio Vista waterfront homes, engineered for wind load, specified for salt air, permitted through Fort Lauderdale and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Back yards that face the water
intro_paragraphs: In Rio Vista the back of the house is the front. Homes on the Rio Vista Isles canals and along the New River look out at deep-water dockage with ocean access through Port Everglades, and everyone here spends the good months outside. So the exterior projects are ambitious: a covered terrace and summer kitchen behind a house on South Rio Vista Boulevard, a pergola and fire feature off a pool deck near Ponce de Leon Drive, a re-poured driveway and fresh stucco so the street elevation finally matches the water side.

Waterfront exteriors pull in more agencies than people expect. Structures, utilities and paving are permitted by Fort Lauderdale Building Services. Seawalls fall under the city's tidal barrier standard in the ULDR, which now sets a minimum top elevation of five feet NAVD in line with the countywide resiliency standard Broward adopted, and seawall, dock or boat-lift work also needs an environmental license from Broward County's environmental permitting division, often with state and federal review behind it. We build the upland side and coordinate with your marine contractor rather than pretending to be one.

The environment out there is harsher than any room inside, so the specification has to be tougher, not looser. That means marine-grade stainless and coated hardware near a canal, dense stone sealed properly, cabinetry actually rated for weather, footings sized by an engineer for wind uplift, and grading that sends a rainy-season downpour toward the drain rather than the slab edge. Utilities get permitted and inspected like any interior trade. The scope is fixed in writing, the site stays clean, and a supervisor is here daily. Lic. CGC1539072.
outdoor-living.scope_heading: Exterior work on a canal lot
outdoor-living.scope_intro: Terrace, kitchen, shade, paving and paint get designed and permitted together, so the yard is torn up once and rebuilt in order.

scope_items.name: A summer kitchen that lasts
scope_items.desc: Permitted gas, water and power out to the terrace, with weather-rated cabinetry and counters that will not chalk out after two seasons on a canal.

scope_items.name: Roofed rooms and trellises
scope_items.desc: Covered outdoor rooms, trellises and shade structures with footings and connections engineered for HVHZ wind loads and detailed to match the house.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and dockside paving
scope_items.desc: Deck rebuilds, pavers and finished concrete laid to positive drainage, with the transition from terrace to seawall cap resolved rather than improvised.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and roofing
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration, color changes and re-roof coordination sequenced with the terrace work, since nobody wants two contractors arguing over one driveway.

scope_items.name: Impact doors to the terrace
scope_items.desc: Sliding and folding glass replaced with HVHZ-approved units, so the wall between the family room and the water opens without weakening the house.

faqs.q: My seawall is old. What does the city require if we replace it?
faqs.a: Fort Lauderdale's land development regulations now set a minimum top elevation of five feet NAVD for new tidal barriers, matching the countywide standard Broward adopted for seawalls and shorelines. In practice that means a replacement usually gets raised rather than rebuilt at its old height, and the terrace behind it has to be regraded to meet the new cap. It is worth planning the upland work and the seawall together instead of twice.

faqs.q: Who has to approve a new dock or boat lift?
faqs.a: More than one agency. The city permits the structure, Broward County's environmental permitting division issues the environmental resource license for work in and around the waterway, and depending on scope the state and the Army Corps may weigh in. Timelines are measured in weeks to months, not days. We are a building contractor, so we coordinate the schedule with a licensed marine contractor and build the terrace, walkway and utilities that meet it.

faqs.q: Do pergolas and summer kitchens really need permits here?
faqs.a: They do. A shade structure is a structure, which means engineered footings, uplift connections and a building permit; the gas, water and electrical serving an outdoor kitchen each carry their own trade permit and inspection. Broward sits in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so wind-load detailing is not a formality. Unpermitted backyard construction tends to surface during a sale, and unwinding it later costs far more than doing it once.

faqs.q: How badly will salt air treat an outdoor kitchen on the canal?
faqs.a: Badly, if the materials are wrong. Standard cabinet boxes, plated hinges and builder-grade fixtures corrode quickly a few feet from brackish water. We specify marine-grade stainless, powder-coated aluminum, stone dense enough to seal on every face, and appliances rated for coastal exposure. Nothing out there is maintenance-free, but a terrace specified correctly on the New River ages along with the house instead of aging like patio furniture.

faqs.q: What should we budget for a full backyard rebuild?
faqs.a: It depends almost entirely on how much of it is structure and utilities. Repaving a terrace is one order of magnitude; a roofed exterior room carrying permitted gas, water, power and drainage is another; adding seawall or dock work in the same season is another again. Finish choices swing the total as much as the footprint does. We price from a site walk and a written specification, never from a per-foot guess.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Walk the property with us, seawall to street. You will get a fixed written scope and a build order that makes sense, in English o en español.
